name: Kingdom of Naples (Bourbon)
native: Regno di Napoli e di Sicilia

predecessors.name: Habsburg monarchy
predecessors.text: the Austrian viceroyalties of Naples and Sicily (1708-1733 for Naples, per the Presidi page), conquered 'by a Spanish army during the War of the Polish Succession in 1734'

successors.name: Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic)
successors.text: the mainland, lost to the French in February 1806

successors.name: Kingdom of the Two Sicilies
successors.text: Sicily, where Ferdinand 'retained his throne' from 1806

rulers.name: Charles of Bourbon (Don Carlos, later Charles III of Spain)

ledger.x: 1735: Charles of Bourbon becomes King of Naples and Sicily.
May 1735: the Presidi pass to the Bourbons.
23 December 1798: Ferdinand flees Naples for Palermo.
21-23 January 1799: the Parthenopean Republic is proclaimed.
28 March 1801: the Treaty of Florence takes the Presidi.
February 1806: the French take the mainland.
1814: the island monarchy is the same state that returns to Naples in 1815.

wars.name: War of the Polish Succession (conquest of Naples and Sicily)
wars.outcome: 'Both Naples and Sicily were conquered by a Spanish army ... in 1734'; the Presidi in May 1735; preliminary peace October 1735; definitive Peace of Vienna, 18 November 1738.

wars.name: French invasion of Naples and the Parthenopean Republic
wars.outcome: French troops took Pescara in December 1798; Ferdinand fled to Palermo on 23 December; the Republic was proclaimed on 21 or 23 January 1799 and fell on 13 June to Ruffo's counter-revolution; Pescara surrendered on 30 June; Ferdinand returned on 10 July.

wars.name: French conquest of the Kingdom of Naples (1806)
wars.outcome: Capua fell on 6 February and Naples on 15 February 1806; Gaeta fell after almost five months; the British won at Maida on 4 July; Ferdinand kept Sicily.

certainty.note: The realm's frontier with the Papal States is the old Neapolitan one (no treaty line is on the pages opened); the Presidi were fixed by the Peace of Vienna (18 November 1738) and the Treaty of Florence (28 March 1801).
